pattern: ^e2e/drivers/motion\.ts chromium › certified/togglebutton\.certified\.spec\.ts › D2 motion \(reduced\) — ToggleButton › default · hover-transition$
reason: Hovering a ToggleButton under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` snaps straight to the hover colours: upstream still runs its two 150 ms transitions there (`background-color` and `color`, `cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.4, 1)`) and the port emits no animation at all. Cosmetic only — the same colours are reached, one frame sooner.

pattern: ^e2e/drivers/motion\.ts chromium › certified/togglebuttongroup\.certified\.spec\.ts › D2 motion \(reduced\) — ToggleButtonGroup › default · hover-transition$
reason: The same defect as the ToggleButton row, on a group item: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the hover colours arrive with no transition where upstream still runs its two 150 ms ones. Cosmetic only — the same colours are reached, one frame sooner.

pattern: ^e2e/drivers/events\.ts chromium › certified/tabs\.certified\.spec\.ts › D4 event sequence — Tabs › horizontal-regular · arrow-next-from-selected$
reason: ArrowRight from the selected tab selects and focuses the next tab, but the roving `tabindex` lands one frame late: for two events of the compared log the old tab still reads `tabindex="0"` and the new one `"-1"`, the reverse of upstream. Keyboard navigation works and settles correctly; a tool that reads tab stops inside that frame sees the previous tab as the stop.
